original_question: Let G be a finite group, Z(p) the localization at p, and Fp the field of p elements. Let X be the class of Fp G-modules obtained by reduction of simple QG-modules. Is it true that Z(p) G is semiperfect if and only if each projective indecomposable Fp G-module can be written as an N-linear combination of modules in X inside the Grothendieck group of Fp G? The “only if” direction is proved, and the affirmative answer is obtained if p does not divide |G| (D. Johnston, D. Rumynin, J. Algebra, 687, no. 1(2026), 776–791).

refined_question: Let p be a prime and G a finite group. Write Z_(p) for the localization of Z at p, and let K_0(F_pG) be the Grothendieck group of finitely generated left F_pG-modules. Let X be the set of Grothendieck classes in K_0(F_pG) arising from reductions modulo p of simple QG-modules. Is it true that the group ring Z_(p)G is semiperfect if and only if, for every projective indecomposable left F_pG-module P, its class [P] lies in the subsemigroup N·X of K_0(F_pG); equivalently, [P] = sum_i n_i[M_i] for some n_i in N and some M_i in X?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 21.60, and your draft already reproduces it very closely.
